priceSnapshot.note: Two things happened since morning and only the second one is on the tape now. Price first ran UP 523.6 points from morning's 63,476.3 mark to 63,999.9 on the 14:00Z bar - through morning's own 63,800 add line, which settled cleanly above at 63,862.0 - and then reversed the entire move and more, flushing to 62,846.3 on the 16:00Z bar. That is a 1,153.6-point round trip inside four hours. The three-day range floor at 63,309.4 that has framed every report since 11 August is GONE: the 16:00Z 1H bar settled 63,165.1, a genuine settle 144.3 points beneath it, not a wick. Price has since bounced 427.1 points off the low and sits at 63,273.4, which is 36.0 points BELOW the broken floor - a retest of it from underneath, unresolved at the time of writing. Settled 1H closes since morning read 63,707.0, 63,721.9, 63,862.0, 63,416.6, 63,165.1: one higher high then three lower closes accelerating.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close below $62,846.3 - the low of this session's flush and the lowest print since 8 August. The distinction from morning's line matters: morning's 63,309.4 was the floor of an intact range and its loss was the question. That question has been answered - the floor broke on a settle - so the reduce line moves down to the low the break actually produced. Price is currently retesting 63,309.4 from below; a settle back beneath 62,846.3 means the retest failed AND the flush low gave way, which is continuation rather than the two-sided chop this range has produced for three days. Note that unlike morning, the map beneath is no longer empty: 62,900 now carries $1,156,589 and 62,800 carries $170,602 of realized mass, so a break there is walking into consumed liquidity rather than the air pocket morning warned about. That makes the move slower, not less real, and it is why this is a reduce trigger and not a stop.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close above $63,625.2 - the 1H EMA20 - with aggregate BTC open interest NOT rising across the same bar. The open-interest condition is carried forward unchanged for the fifth consecutive session because it keeps doing its job: it separates a move that is being bought from one that is being covered. The price has moved DOWN from morning's 63,800 for a specific reason rather than a loosening of standards. 63,800 has now been tested and rejected within this session - the 14:00Z bar settled 63,862.0 above it and price was 1,015.9 points lower two bars later - so it is no longer the first gate on the way up, it is the second. The first is the 1H EMA20 at 63,625.17, which price has not closed above since the 14:00Z bar and which sits 351.8 points overhead. A settle back above it says the breakdown was a liquidity grab; anything less is a bounce inside a broken structure.

decisionBox.changed: Position moves from morning's REDUCE to HOLD on spot, and the bearish view is expressed in a small futures hedge instead. That is not a softening - the read is more bearish than morning's, not less - it is a refusal to sell the low of a completed flush. The reasoning is specific. Morning trimmed 17% of the bag at 63,476.3 and that trim is 202.9 points in front at the mark, so the tactical reduction is already done and it worked. What has changed since is that the range broke on a settle: the 16:00Z 1H bar closed 63,165.1, 144.3 points below the 63,309.4 floor, and the low printed 62,846.3. Every 1H exponential average remains overhead - EMA20 63,625.17, EMA50 63,758.12, EMA100 63,985.71, EMA200 64,034.37 - and the 1H MACD has now crossed negative exactly as morning forecast it would within one to two bars: line -54.75 under signal -21.16, histogram -33.59 against morning's +30.81. The daily MACD line has gone negative too, -45.15 against morning's +17.28, which is the first time the daily line has been beneath zero this month. Positioning has deteriorated further: realized liquidations run $6,033,533 of longs against $2,075,715 of shorts, a 2.91 ratio widened from morning's 2.72, and the OKX long/short account ratio fell to 1.79 at the 14:00Z high and has climbed 1.80, 1.84, 1.87 on the three reads through the flush - retail longs re-loading into weakness for the second consecutive session. Against all of that sits one genuine improvement that argues against selling here: the air pocket morning identified beneath 63,309.4 has been FILLED. Morning's map showed $278,478 at 63,300 and then nothing to 63,000. This map shows $1,027,868 at 63,200, $346,538 at 63,100, $1,025,068 at 63,000 and $1,156,589 at 62,900. The vacuum was traded through and is now consumed mass. Selling spot into a level that has just absorbed $3.5m of forced supply is selling the wrong side of the flush, so the core is held and the short is where the risk gets taken - with a stop 306.6 points away rather than an open-ended one.

liquidation.note: $1,673,002 of realized swap liquidations, still the single heaviest bucket on the map for the third consecutive session and roughly 1.45x the next one. It barely grew from morning's $1,663,406, which is the informative part: price traded THROUGH 63,800 in both directions this session - up to 63,999.9 and back down - without adding meaningful forced supply there, meaning the shelf was already cleared out this morning and the round trip was positioning, not liquidation. The standing caveat applies: this is REALIZED mass, liquidity already consumed, not resting orders overhead. Its use is as the magnet and as the marker of the level a genuine repair still has to settle back above.

$1,156,589 - and this bucket did not exist in any meaningful size on morning's map, which showed the region below 63,300 as empty down to 63,000. It was built entirely by the 16:00Z flush to 62,846.3. This is the single most important change on the board: the air pocket morning warned about has been traded through and converted into consumed mass. It sits 373.4 points below spot and is the floor of the reduce trigger.

$1,027,868, immediately beneath spot at 73.4 points below. Also newly heavy - morning's map had nothing at this level. It marks where longs were force-sold on the way down through the range floor and is the first measured support a continuation would have to re-break.

liquidityMagnet.note: Freshness is not in doubt: the newest fill is timestamped 17:45:56Z, roughly ninety seconds before the read, and it printed at 63,274.4 - within a dollar of spot at 63,273.4. The feed is live. The headline change is the SHAPE of the map rather than any single level. Morning measured $4,237,221 above spot against $1,120,747 below, a 3.8-to-1 skew that made the downside look like a vacuum. This read measures $4,382,586 above (63,300 through 64,000) against $3,726,665 below (62,800 through 63,200), a 1.18-to-1 skew. The pull is BALANCED, and it got there because the flush to 62,846.3 built $2,528,195 of new mass in the 62,900-63,100 band that simply did not exist this morning. Read that correctly: it is not bullish, because all of it is consumed liquidity by construction and it accumulated precisely BECAUSE price fell through it. What it does mean is that the specific risk morning flagged - a 309-point air pocket with no measured mass to slow a break - has been spent. The next leg down, if it comes, grinds rather than gaps.

The forming 17:00Z bar has a high of 63,298.2, which is a LOWER high than the 16:00Z bar's 63,571.4 - the bounce is losing its own momentum at the retest.

The EMA200 reclaim is dead and the settled record now says so plainly. Morning flagged the forming 08:00Z bar as the board's most important unresolved question - whether it would settle as an outside-down bar giving back the reclaim. It settled 63,475.9, below the EMA200 at 63,722.97, and the 12:00Z bar that followed settled 63,416.6, lower again. Two consecutive settles beneath the line ends the repair that midnight sized on. The averages are bearishly stacked overhead - EMA20 63,881.87, EMA50 64,137.85, EMA100 64,159.10 - and the EMA200 at 63,722.97 has flipped from support to the 449.6-point resistance immediately above. RSI 39.89, down from morning's 46.14. The MACD histogram at -23.82 is fractionally wider than morning's -20.24 with the line falling to -272.87. The forming 16:00Z bar is the one to watch: it opened 63,416.7, reached 63,571.4, printed 62,846.3 and trades 63,273.4, so it is currently a long-legged hammer with a 427.1-point lower wick. If it settles near here that wick is a genuine rejection of the lows and the first constructive candle on this timeframe in three days. It settles at 20:00Z, well before the endday session.

One real deterioration on top of a week of unchanged bearish context. The unchanged part: price is below all four daily averages with the EMA20 at 64,106.21 sitting 832.8 points overhead, the EMA50 at 64,535.49 1,262.1 above, the EMA100 at 66,655.00 5.3% above and the EMA200 at 72,450.33 14.5% above. That last figure is the frame every intraday read on this page sits inside. The change is the MACD line: it has gone NEGATIVE at -45.15 against morning's +17.28, the first sub-zero daily reading this month, with the signal still at 58.27 and the histogram widening to -103.43 from -66.85. A daily MACD line crossing beneath zero after a bear cross is the momentum confirmation the daily chart had been withholding. RSI 44.95. Note the convention: OKX daily bars roll at 16:00Z, so the last settled bar is 12 August at 63,416.6 and the forming one carries a 63,571.4 high and a 62,846.3 low. Daily ATR(14) is 1,286.51, which is 2.03% - the entire 1,167.9-point range this report is parsing is still smaller than one average daily bar.

liquidations.note: 799 filled swap liquidations across 2026-08-12T18:19:24Z to 2026-08-13T17:45:56Z: longs $6,033,533 against shorts $2,075,715, a ratio of 2.91 that has widened again from morning's 2.72 and midnight's 1.18. Longs are now being taken out at nearly three times the rate of shorts and the newest fill printed at 63,274.4, within a dollar of spot - the liquidation is happening at the current price, not at an old level. The skew field carries the OKX long/short ACCOUNT ratio at 1.87 (17:00Z read) rather than the USD ratio, per the field's definition, and it repeats this morning's pattern with unusual clarity. The ten hourly reads run 1.74, 1.76, 1.76, 1.88, 1.87, 1.83, 1.79, 1.80, 1.84, 1.87: the ratio fell to 1.79 exactly at the 14:00Z session HIGH of 63,999.9, meaning longs took profit into strength, and then climbed on all three reads through the flush to 62,846.3, meaning they bought the decline. That is the second consecutive session of retail adding longs into weakness and it is the configuration that keeps supplying fuel for the next leg. Set against it, the book as a whole continues to shrink rather than lever up: BTC-USDT-SWAP open interest is $2,055,737,216 against morning's $2,069,669,656, -0.67%, aggregate BTC open interest is $2,643,038,074 at the 17:00Z read against $2,686,318,644 this morning, -1.61%, and funding is flat at +0.00813% per 8h against morning's +0.00816%. Flat funding through a 1,153-point round trip is notable in its own right: nobody is paying up for either side. The synthesis is a smaller, more long-crowded book being ground down rather than a leveraged blow-off.

indices.note: Last daily close 723.70 on 12 August, +0.73%. The 13 August US session IS open at the time of this report - unlike morning, when it had not yet started - and it is the single most striking data point on the page: QQQ is trading 732.66 intraday, +1.24% and +8.96 on the day, with an intraday high of 733.76 against a 52-week high of 748.65. While Bitcoin was flushing through a three-day range floor to 62,846.3, the Nasdaq proxy was making a fresh monthly high. The cross-asset divergence midnight, morning and endday have each flagged in turn has not merely widened, it has inverted into two markets telling opposite stories on the same afternoon. For a crypto book that reads as a risk asset, that is the most uncomfortable fact available: the risk-on bid is real and it is going somewhere other than here.

calibration.rollingRecord: 2 of the last 9 rated sessions helped. The two yes marks are 12 August midnight and 13 August morning; 11 August morning/midday/endday, 12 August morning/midday/endday and 13 August midnight are all no. This is the first session in six where acting at the mark has paid, and it paid because the action was a REDUCTION rather than an addition - the desk's four losing trades in that window were all adds or trims in the wrong direction, while the one that worked cut exposure ahead of a break that then happened.
calibration.note: Morning's two published levels BOTH fired, in the awkward order, and the honest reading of that is a whipsaw rather than a success. The add line at 63,800 fired first and fired on fully valid mechanics: the 14:00Z 1H bar settled 63,862.0, 62.0 points above the line, and aggregate BTC open interest fell from $2,688,568,878 to $2,679,314,772 across that same bar, satisfying both halves of the composite trigger. Two bars later price was at 62,846.3, 1,015.7 points lower. Then the reduce line at 63,309.4 fired on the 16:00Z bar, which settled 63,165.1, a genuine settle 144.3 points through it. A desk that had mechanically obeyed both triggers would have bought 63,862.0 and sold 63,165.1 inside two hours, for -697 points. That is the single most important lesson available from this session and it is not about direction: composite triggers that fire on a spike into a level, in a range that is actively breaking, produce the worst possible fills. The TRADE, however, was right and is the first winner in six sessions. Morning reduced 17% of the spot bag at 63,476.3; the mark is 63,273.4, so the trim is 202.9 points in front, +0.32% on the trimmed notional. It also survived a 523.6-point adverse excursion to 63,999.9 before working, which is worth recording - the trade was underwater for two hours and would have been stopped out by anyone managing it tightly.
